questions.question: Ahmadnagar was finally annexed by the Mughals in _____.
questions.solution:
• Year: 1632
  • Ruler: Annexed during the reign of Shah Jahan after years of struggle.

questions.question: ‘Do or die’ slogan is given by which of the following freedom fighter?
questions.solution:
• Leader: Mahatma Gandhi
  • Context: Delivered during the Quit India Movement in 1942.

questions.question: The Paris Indian Society was an Indian nationalist organisation founded in ______.
questions.solution:
• Year: 1905
  • Founder: Madam Bhikaiji Cama was one of the key leaders associated with this revolutionary group in France.

questions.question: Manimekalai describes the story of which of the following?
questions.solution:
• Story: Kovalan and Madhavi's Daughter
  • Poem: It is a sequel to the Tamil epic Silappadikaram.

questions.question: “A History of British India” is a work Published by ______.
questions.solution:
• Author: James Mill
  • Philosophy: A Scottish economist who divided Indian history into Hindu, Muslim, and British periods.

questions.question: Which of the following dynasty was not the part of "tripartite struggle", which fought for centuries to control over one particularly prized area Kanauj?
questions.solution:
• Non-Participant: Kadamba
  • Conflict: The struggle involved the Palas (East), Pratiharas (North/West), and Rashtrakutas (South).

questions.question: Rajaraja I and Rajendra I belonged to the ____________ dynasty.
questions.solution:
• Dynasty: Chola
  • Legacy: They expanded the empire to Southeast Asia and built the Brihadisvara Temple.

questions.question: Which of the following was “NOT” a main centre of Revolt of 1857?
questions.solution:
• Not a Centre: Rohtak
  • Centres: Delhi, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi, and Bareilly were the primary hotspots.

questions.question: How many delegates participated in the second session of Indian National Congress?
questions.solution:
• Delegates: 434
  • Context: Held in Calcutta (1886) and presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji.

questions.question: Thanjavur was the capital of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Capital: Chola
  • Fact: Famous for its Chola architecture and the Great Living Chola Temples.

questions.question: Warren Hastings became the first Governor General of India in which year?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1773
  • Act: Appointed under the Regulating Act of 1773.

questions.question: In ancient times, the area to the south of the Ganga was known as______.
questions.solution:
• Region: Magadha
  • Power: It became the most powerful Mahajanapada due to its fertile land and iron mines.

questions.question: Which of the following Chola ruler built a temple for goddess Nishumbhasudini?
questions.solution:
• Goddess: Nishumbhasudini
  • Context: Built by Vijayalaya after he conquered Thanjavur.

questions.question: When did the Indian Independence Act receive the British royal assent?
questions.solution:
• Month: July 1947
  • Date: 18th July 1947; it provided for the partition of India and Pakistan.

questions.question: Which of the following region was the capital of the Chalukyas?
questions.solution:
• Capital: Aihole
  • Fact: Known as the 'Cradle of Indian Temple Architecture'.

questions.question: Fa Xian began his journey back home from which of the following Indian state?
questions.solution:
• Departure: Bengal
  • Journey: He took a ship from the port of Tamralipti in Bengal.

questions.question: Fa Xian began his journey back home from which of the following Indian state?
questions.solution:
• Departure (Repeat): Bengal
  • Note: He spent years collecting Buddhist texts before leaving via the sea route.

questions.question: In the ____________, Sarojini Naidu persuaded Mahatma Gandhi to allow women to join the movement.
questions.solution:
• Movement: Salt Satyagraha (1930)
  • Impact: Her persuasion led to massive female participation in the freedom struggle.

questions.question: Subsidiary alliance treaty was imposed on Awadh in ______.
questions.solution:
• Year: 1801
  • Terms: Lord Wellesley forced the Nawab of Awadh to surrender half his territory to the British.

questions.question: Minhaj-i-Siraj was a chronicler during the rule of ______.
questions.solution:
• Ruler: Sultan Iltutmish
  • Fact: Minhaj wrote the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, a valuable source for the early Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of ‘Dynasty - Ruled region’ is correctly matched? I. Shakas - North west and north India II. Vakatakas - Central and western India
questions.solution:
• Correct Match: Both I and II
  • Regional Powers: Shakas dominated the Northwest, while Vakatakas were the successors to the Satavahanas in the Deccan.

questions.question: Chittaranjan Das was the political guru of which of the following personalities?
questions.solution:
• Personal Guru: Subhash Chandra Bose
  • Fact: Bose referred to C.R. Das as 'Deshbandhu'.

questions.question: “All India Muslim League” was formed at Dacca in ______.
questions.solution:
• Year: 1906
  • Context: Formed during the Dacca Session to advocate for separate electorates for Muslims.

questions.question: The iron pillar situated at Mehrauli, Delhi is belonged to which of the following Gupta ruler?
questions.solution:
• Ruler: Chandragupta II
  • Mystery: The pillar is famous for its rust-resistant composition, showcasing advanced ancient metallurgy.

questions.question: The early Turkish rulers ruled between _____ years over Delhi.
questions.solution:
• Period: 1206 and 1290
  • Rulers: Also known as the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty, starting with Qutbuddin Aibak.
